subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — damage cap framing & carve-outs
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenny Park <jenny.park@novacorp.com>, contracts@novacorp.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (liability cap ask)

Marissa —

Thanks for the call earlier. We attached our redlines to the MSA and Order Form for the Renewal deal (see Novacorp_MSA_redline.docx / OrderForm_Redline.xlsx). Two items we need to make progress on so Procurement/Legal can sign off:

1) Liability cap: Novacorp prefers a cap equal to 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months (measured on an invoice basis), with an annual reset rather than an aggregate across the entire term. This aligns to how our vendors manage exposure for multi-year contracts.

2) Consequential damages: we are OK preserving a limited consequential damages carve-out but would like a mutual carve that excludes direct financial loss only; we would still expect intellectual property infringement/indemnity and willful misconduct to be carved out.

We are trying to avoid a high fixed-dollar cap (e.g., $1M flat) because our average annual spend on this contract is material to us — applying a multiplier keeps the cap proportional. Please review and let us know if Redwood has a comparable framing you can share so we can get this to Legal.

Next steps: can you propose a short compromise that your Legal team can accept? We are aiming to finalize this week.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Procurement, Novacorp
samir.patel@novacorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacorp.com>
Cc: Jenny Park <jenny.park@novacorp.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (liability cap ask)

Samir —

Appreciate the clear framing and the redlines. I’ve looped in our legal (Laura) and pricing lead (Karthik) to propose a concise counterproposal that balances proportionality with predictable exposure for Redwood. High level:

- Redwood preference: liability cap defined as the greater of $1,000,000 (USD) or 3x the fees paid in the preceding 12 months, measured on an invoiced basis, with an annual reset. That keeps the vendor protected on smaller deals while scaling to larger customers.

- Consequential damages: Redwood maintains a mutual consequential-damages exclusion but will carve out claims arising from Redwood’s breach of confidentiality (data breach), IP infringement indemnity, and claims resulting from gross negligence or willful misconduct.

- Want to avoid a contract-term cumulative cap (we prefer an annual reset tied to invoice window) because it’s operationally simpler for forecasting and aligns with our billing cadence.

I’m attaching our standard cap language (Redwood_Cap_Terms.pdf) to show the precise wording we typically use. Laura — can you take a look and suggest modifications we should expect Novacorp Legal to push back on? Karthik — flag if the multiplier is something we can flex on (2x vs 3x vs 4x) depending on order value.

Samir/Jenny — if you can confirm whether Novacorp will accept an "annual reset" measurement (12-month lookback on invoices) that would help us present a clean counter. I’ll propose a consolidated redline once Legal confirms.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0133

Attachments: Redwood_Cap_Terms.pdf (standard language)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (liability cap ask)

Marissa / Karthik —

I reviewed Novacorp’s redlines and Marissa’s suggested position. My legal read and recommended counter (short bullets):

- Cap amount: propose greater of $1,500,000 or 4x fees paid in the preceding 12 months for strategic/enterprise customers. Rationale: proportionate exposure while preserving a meaningful floor for situations where invoiced fees are low.

- Measurement window: accept a 12-month lookback measured on an invoice basis, but clarify that the measurement date is the date of breach or discovery, with the calculation based on the 12 months preceding that date. This prevents manipulation of invoice timing.

- Aggregate vs annual reset: recommend annual reset (rolling 12 months) rather than a cumulative contract-term cap. Cumulative caps create unpredictability and can be gamed with early terminations or trial periods. Annual reset with defined measurement date is cleaner for both parties.

- Carve-outs: accept IP infringement and willful misconduct as carve-outs; add explicit carve-out for breaches of confidentiality resulting in unauthorized data exfiltration. Keep gross negligence and indemnity-related obligations uncapped.

- Consequential damages: maintain a mutual exclusion but include limited carve-outs that track the indemnity/IP/confidentiality exceptions. Suggest concrete sample language for the indemnity carve: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, damages arising from (i) Redwood’s breach of confidentiality resulting in unauthorized disclosure or exfiltration of Customer Data, (ii) Redwood’s willful misconduct or gross negligence, or (iii) claims for intellectual property infringement indemnified under this Agreement shall not be subject to the limitations or exclusions in this Section."

Operational note: if Procurement insists on a pure multiplier approach (2x) we can consider tiered concessions — lower multiplier for small customers with a higher fixed floor for enterprise. Karthik, please advise acceptable thresholds for enterprise vs standard deals.

I’ll prepare a redlined MSA snippet and a one-page memo explaining the legal rationale for Marissa to send to Novacorp.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: Legal_Counter_Draft.docx (draft language + rationale)

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (liability cap ask) — consolidated counterproposal

Samir / Novacorp Legal —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is our consolidated counter redline (MSA_OrderForm_Redline_Consolidated.docx) and a short note on why this approach is mutually practical. High-level offer:

- Liability cap = greater of $1,500,000 (USD) or 3x fees paid in the preceding 12 months (invoiced basis), with a rolling 12-month measurement (annual reset).

- Measurement date: the date of the event giving rise to the claim (we will look back at the prior 12 months of invoices to calculate the multiplier).

- Carve-outs: IP infringement indemnity, willful misconduct, gross negligence, and breaches of confidentiality resulting in unauthorized data exfiltration are excluded from the cap.

- Consequential damages: mutual exclusion remains, subject to the carve-outs above.

Rationale: this gets both parties’ objectives — a proportional cap that scales with spend (you’re protected from a tiny flat cap on a large contract) while preserving meaningful protection for Redwood. We moved from 4x -> 3x and kept a material fixed floor to show flexibility on both sides.

If Novacorp Legal can accept the language in the attached redline, we can finalize the Order Form and route to DocuSign. If you’d like a short call to walk through the carve-outs I’m happy to join — otherwise please confirm in writing and we’ll issue an updated order form.

Marissa Cole
